reviewPolicy: Production timers must name why they are scheduler-safe or why they remain legacy debt.

timers.justification: Session roles change outside editor events; this small status clock is cleared on departure and page teardown.
Yields once so a burst of selections settles before any text is materialized; it only resolves a promise, and the abort signal is checked right after.
Debounces outline requests in the demo app; the handle is cleared before each reschedule, and a stale load is dropped by its generation.
Benchmark settle between phases: it only resolves the awaited promise, so deferred editor work finishes before reads are counted.
Benchmark observation of the first animation frame after an applied key; it records a timestamp only, tracks the frame handle, and cancels pending frames on disposal.

The bounded churn benchmark yields to the browser every ten iterations so cancellation and rendering can run. The timer only resolves the awaited promise; the next iteration checks cancellation before editing.
Benchmark harness: one frame between batches keeps them apart.
Benchmark harness: two frames let the editor mount before any pass is timed.

Benchmark observation of input dispatch completion after synchronous edit callbacks return. The enabled guard drops observations after disposal; measuring this boundary through the editor scheduler would change the interval being measured.
Benchmark observation of the next animation frame after input dispatch. It records a timestamp only, tracks each frame handle, and cancels pending frames when the probe is disposed.
Harness readiness and cleanup only: the shared deadline bounds worker awaits outside captured input; the timer is cleared when the stage settles.
Harness readiness only: polling yields for states without a completion event, outside captured input and within the caller's absolute deadline.
Fixture socket open is delivered once after construction so the client can install listeners. The callback checks the connecting state and becomes inert after close; it schedules no further work.

Fixture initialize response is delivered once after send so the RPC caller can register its pending request. The callback checks the open state and becomes inert after close; it schedules no further work.
Simulated source latency for the paged proof; it only resolves the awaited read, and the abort signal is checked right after.

timers.justification: Authorization may never settle; the deadline bounds reserved quota, and finally clears it and releases the reservation when upgrade fails.
Silent clients emit no progress event; one deadline per socket bounds subscription and application idle time, is replaced by progress, and is cleared on close.
BroadcastChannel has no remote-close or crash event; this heartbeat expires silent peers and advertises membership, and close clears the interval.
The protocol needs elapsed time for failure detection; this opt-in clock is configurable, manual in simulations, and cleared when its view detaches.
Remote presence changes between editor updates; one frame coalesces its notifications into a paint, and disposal cancels the pending frame.
Peer events cannot signal elapsed idle time; each view keeps one deadline for the next visible name's idle transition, and clear or disposal cancels it.
Remote broker readiness has no notification; one retry per URL spaces reconnect attempts, connect checks closed, and close clears every pending retry.
Signaling has no peer-roster notification; discovery announcements and retries expire silent peers on this protocol clock, which close clears.
A TURN supplier may never settle; abort bounds the wait, finally clears the deadline, and close aborts pending requests.
Native connection setup can stall without a terminal event; channel open or removal clears this deadline, and failure checks the current link generation.
A child can emit neither readiness nor exit; this bounds startup failure, while stdout readiness, error, and exit notifications each clear the deadline.

Nothing to animate still has to finish asynchronously, or a caller that always sees its completion after returning would see it before returning on an empty document. Guarded by `stopped`, so a cancel between the two beats it.

Drives a fixed-duration decorative overlay at a tick computed from its own duration, and owns the matching `clearInterval` in `stop()`. It paints a layer above the rows rather than editor state, so nothing it does has to be ordered against document work.
Fires the completion callback when no animation was started, so a caller hears about it in the same turn ordering either way.
This is the frame scheduler every caller goes through; the handle is returned so the owner cancels it on disposal.
Stands in for a frame where no window provides one (workers, tests); cancellable through the same handle as the frame path.
The scheduler owns this task budget deadline. Expiry checks task identity before aborting; completion, failure, cancellation, and disposal clear the budget timer.
The scheduler owns one deferred queue flush at a time, selects current tasks by priority, and drops cancelled or replaced work before starting it. Disposal clears the queue timer and queued work.

The scheduler owns delayed task starts and clamps repeated scheduling to the requested maximum delay. Cancellation and disposal clear the handle; task identity and stale-result checks guard execution and application.

Coalesces the demand signal against the viewport rather than against rendering. `'viewport'` is fired once per scroll event and is not throttled at source, so a flung scroll is one update per frame; `cancel()` on every input is what turns that into one question per pause. The delay itself is the host's number — this editor names none.

Runs once per highlighter after a one-second delay so background grammar preload stays behind latency-sensitive tokenization and its first paint. `backgroundLoaded` prevents duplicate schedules, and worker-task tracking keeps idle fences and teardown behind the preload.
Coalesces the re-registration one engine needs to repaint highlights to once per registry per turn; `pendingRegistries` is what makes a second call in the same turn a no-op rather than a second pass.
Expires a one-frame measurement cache at the next frame; it only deletes the entry, so a stale callback after disposal is harmless.

Measuring every row's width is the work the horizontal scroll extent needs and nothing on screen is waiting for, so it is deliberately given whatever the frame has left rather than a place in the queue. `cancelContentWidthMeasurement` withdraws it when the content it would measure has already changed.
The same deferral for an engine with no idle callback. Zero rather than a delay, because the point is only to leave the current frame, and the same cancel withdraws it.

Leaving the current frame is the entire content of this delay: it is what keeps the repaint out of the resize delivery and out of the row paint that ask for it. The one outstanding handle per view makes a second request in the same frame a no-op, and `cancelInlineWidgetRepaint` withdraws it when the view goes away.

Debounces a question to the language server against the caret and the diagnostics, not against rendering, and `clear()` withdraws it on every further change — so a fix is never computed against text the reader has already moved past.
Phase 0 legacy baseline; keep until Phase 3 scheduler migration or replace with a specific scheduler-owned justification.
Debounces a request to the language server against the caret, not against rendering, and `cancel()` clears it on every move — so the server sees one question per pause rather than one per keystroke.

Coalesces the re-indents a single keystroke can queue into one pass at the end of the turn, so the edit lands before the frame the character was typed in is painted; `scheduled` is what makes a second call in that turn a no-op rather than a second pass.
A reconnect backoff, not rendering work: the handle is kept, cleared on dispose, and a disposed connection ignores it.

Replays pooled connection state after `acquire` returns so callbacks cannot run inside the contribution constructor. The closure verifies that the lease is still active, and each acquisition schedules at most one replay.

Keeps a connection reusable for the configured grace period after its final lease releases. A new acquisition cancels the timer, and `#closeIdle` rechecks both the lease count and pool identity before disposal.
Phase 0 legacy baseline; keep until Phase 3 scheduler migration or replace with a specific scheduler-owned justification.

timers.justification: Yields once per MiB so indexing a large source never holds the thread; it only resolves the awaited promise, and the next page read carries the lifetime signal.
Caps how long a hover waits for tokens before painting plain; it only resolves the losing side of a race.
Enforces the hover dwell before paint; the pointer leaving the target clears it.
Delays the loading row until the participants are observably slow; every target change cancels it.
Starts server work midway through the pointer dwell so transient targets are skipped while network time overlaps the rest of the dwell.
A pointer grace period before the hover goes away, cancelled by re-entry; it schedules no editor work.
Resets the copy button's label after the user has had time to read it; DOM only.
Defers the callback past StrictMode's synchronous replay; the incarnation, document and state guards drop it when the editor moved on, and no editor work is scheduled.
Waits out React's synchronous StrictMode unmount and remount; the generation guard drops the disposal when the component came straight back.
Defers delivery until the mount survives React's synchronous StrictMode replay; the incarnation guard cancels disposed mounts, and no editor work is scheduled.

Yields one macrotask so the visible result reaches its caller before complete analysis enters the worker queue; it only resolves the awaited promise, and the abort signal is checked before source preparation.
Yields one macrotask between warm-up compiles so a parse or edit message queued meanwhile runs before the next language; worker-task tracking keeps idle fences behind warm-up.

timers.justification: Runs once after the parse answer is posted; it re-checks that the document is still cached and idle, so a late or stale callback does nothing.
A request timeout inside the worker: it only rejects the pending request, and the answer clears it.

Debounces diagnostics per document inside the worker, off the main thread; the handle is kept per URI and cleared on the next edit or close.
